title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This page opens §1 of a set of notes on de Rham cohomology. Page 20 is a title page: 'Coh de De Rham … (à caractéristiques diverses)'. The page lays the algebraic foundations for divided powers, the basic tool of crystalline cohomology.

(1) Definition of a pseudo-ring. A pseudo-ring is an abelian group with an associative bilinear multiplication; in modern terms, a non-unital ring. Commutativity is assumed from here on.

(2) Definition of a pseudo-ring with divided powers. This is a pseudo-ring with maps π^n: x ↦ x^{(n)} for n ≥ 1, subject to five axioms:
- 1.1: π^1 = id.
- 1.2: π^n(x+y) = π^n(x) + Σ_{p,q≥1, p+q=n} π^p(x)π^q(y) + π^n(y).
- 1.3: π^n(xy) = x^n π^n(y).
- 1.4: π^m(π^n(x)) = (mn)!/((n!)^m m!) · π^{mn}(x).
- 1.5: π^m(x)π^n(x) = (m+n)!/(m!n!) · π^{m+n}(x).
The point of working without a unit is that the divided powers γ_0 = 1 never has to be part of the structure. The structure lives intrinsically on the ideal J, not on the ambient ring.

(3) The ideal case. When J is an ideal of a ring A, with the induced pseudo-ring structure, 1.2 becomes the usual formula π^n(x+y) = Σ_{p+q=n} π^p(x)π^q(y). This uses the conventions π^0 = 1 and π^p = 0 for p < 0.

(4) Consequences. By induction, 1.5 gives the multinomial formula 1.5.bis: π^{p_1}(x)⋯π^{p_r}(x) = (Σp_i)!/(∏p_i!) · π^{Σp_i}(x). Taking all p_i = 1 and using 1.1 gives 1.5.ter: n! π^n(x) = x^n.

(5) Linear version (continued on p.22). The page ends by starting the Λ-linear version. Over a base ring Λ one requires the homogeneity π^n(λx) = λ^n π^n(x); this is axiom 1.6 on the next page. The next page notes this is automatic over ℤ. A PD-ideal J ⊂ A is then a homogeneous PD pseudo-ring structure on the A-algebra J. §2 (next page) begins the construction of the canonical PD structure on Γ_A(M), extending x ↦ x^{(n)} via (x^{(p)})^{(n)} = (pn)!/((p!)^n n!) · x^{(pn)}.

Purpose: these are the standard foundations for PD-envelopes, crystals and crystalline/de Rham comparison, i.e. the setting later written up by Berthelot.
errors: No mathematical errors: the coefficients in 1.4, 1.5, 1.5.bis and the derivation of 1.5.ter are correct.

Gap, not an error: for an ideal J ⊂ A, axiom 1.3 only gives homogeneity with respect to multipliers x ∈ J. The usual PD axiom γ_n(λx) = λ^n γ_n(x) for all λ ∈ A is not yet imposed. Grothendieck adds it on the next page as axiom 1.6 (A-algebra homogeneity), noting it is automatic over ℤ.

ideas.what: Divided power structure on a non-unital commutative ring (pseudo-ring), axioms 1.1–1.5
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Cartan (Séminaire Cartan 1954–55); N. Roby (1963–65); Berthelot (1974)
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA as such. The theory appears in Berthelot's thesis (LNM 407), which was developed from Grothendieck's ideas (1966 letter to Tate, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' in Dix exposés).

ideas.what: Reduction of the sum axiom to Σ_{p+q=n} γ_p(x)γ_q(y) in the ideal case, with conventions γ_0 = 1 and γ_p = 0 for p < 0
ideas.modern_name: Standard PD axioms for an ideal

ideas.what: Multinomial identity and n! γ_n(x) = x^n
ideas.modern_name: Elementary consequences of the PD axioms

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard axiomatization of divided powers, phrased for non-unital rings in the Cartan–Roby style. It is historically interesting as Grothendieck's own working foundations for crystalline/de Rham cohomology, but nothing here goes beyond what Cartan, Roby and Berthelot published.
transcription_corrections: In the heading the inserted mark reads 'Pseudo-anneau J/ à puissances divisées'. The 'J' (or similar) is an insertion caret/annotation, and the underlined phrases are 'à puissances divisées'.
'la relation 2.' and 'la formule 5.' refer to axioms 1.2 and 1.5.
In 1.2 a blotted-out symbol precedes π^n(x), apparently a deleted coefficient.
In 1.5.ter the image shows overwritten scribbles, apparently 'n! π^n(x)^{(…)} = … x^n' with deletions. The intended formula is n! π^n(x) = x^n.
In 1.3 the image reads 'π^n(xy) = x^n π^n(y)', confirming the transcription.
The last line reads 'Soit Λ un anneau (commutatif), une Λ-algèbre…', with the first word overwritten.
